# DSP Architecture: LinkGrabber

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. LinkGrabber has NO DSP. "Stage 2 / dsp-agent work" in this document means the non-audio engine: state, history store, tool management, download pipeline, drag-out. Stage 1 builds the passthrough shell; Stage 3 is the native GUI.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent)
**Date:** 2026-11-07
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation + Shell), Stage 2 (engine), Stage 3 (GUI)
**Purpose:** Specification of a silent-passthrough utility that downloads YouTube audio with external `yt-dlp` + `ffmpeg` (MP3 320 kbps or WAV 24-bit), shows progress as a Minesweeper board, keeps a persisted download history, and drags finished files into the DAW.

**Complexity tier:** 5 (non-DSP: child processes, file I/O, persisted history, OS drag-and-drop, external tool management). **Research depth:** DEEP.

**Evidence legend:**
- VERIFIED-HEADER: checked in the JUCE 8.0.12 sources at `/Users/solomonraileanu/JUCE/modules`.
- VERIFIED-PRIOR: observed in this repo's earlier LinkGrab work (git commits `309b89c`, `f1c3063`, `4f5f7e7`, `beed806`; reference notes and `.continue-here.md` in that history).
- WEB: found by web search (secondary sources, forum posts, project READMEs). Not an official guarantee.
- UNVERIFIED: reasoning only; must be proven by a test in the phase named next to it.

**Prior art reused (fresh design, but with these lessons):** LinkGrab (removed in `fb10a0f`) reached a working extractor with a native Minesweeper UI, a processor-owned `DownloadManager`, and a `DownloadCommand.h` of pure helpers (link validation, argv builder, incremental output parser, failure classifier). Console tests drove MP3 320k, WAV `pcm_s24le`, bad link, unavailable video, cancel and destroy-mid-download successfully. It was NEVER tested for drag-out inside any DAW and NEVER rendered visually. Its host test showed that inside Logic Pro (AU, hosted out-of-process by `AUHostingServiceXPC_arrow`) `/usr/bin/true`, `yt-dlp --version`, `ffmpeg -version` all ran via `/usr/bin/env PATH=... ` and writing to `~/Music/LinkGrab` succeeded (VERIFIED-PRIOR). A real download inside a host was not tested.

**Environment facts (this machine, checked 2026-11-07):** `/opt/homebrew/bin` contains `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg`, `deno`. JUCE is 8.0.12. With `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (what a Finder-launched DAW provides) yt-dlp warns that no JavaScript runtime is available; with `/opt/homebrew/bin` on PATH deno is found (VERIFIED-PRIOR).

## Core Components

### 1. Passthrough Audio Path
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioProcessor` (module `juce_audio_processors`); no `juce::dsp` classes
- **Purpose:** Pass host audio through untouched so the plugin can sit on any track or the master
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:**
  - `BusesProperties().withInput("Input", stereo, true).withOutput("Output", stereo, true)` in the constructor (critical pattern #4). `IS_SYNTH FALSE` (pattern #22), no MIDI
  - `isBusesLayoutSupported`: mono/mono and stereo/stereo, input set == output set
  - `processBlock`: audio already in place; only clear output channels beyond the input channel count. No allocation, no locks, no logging, no ValueTree/APVTS string access. `ScopedNoDenormals` unnecessary (no arithmetic)
  - `getLatencySamples() == 0`, `getTailLengthSeconds() == 0`
  - `NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER FALSE` (native UI; patterns #3, #8, #9, #11, #13, #21 do not apply)

### 2. Plugin State (format parameter + session extras)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState` with one `AudioParameterChoice`; extra non-parameter properties on the APVTS state `ValueTree` (modules `juce_audio_processors`, `juce_data_structures`)
- **Purpose:** Persist `format` (MP3 320 / WAV 24-bit), the last pasted `link`, and `outputFolder` across editor close and host session save/load
- **Parameters Affected:** `format`
- **Configuration:**
  - `format`: `AudioParameterChoice`, ID `format`, choices `{"MP3 320 kbps","WAV 24-bit"}`, default 0. Declared NON-automatable with `AudioProcessorValueTreeState::ParameterAttributes().withAutomatable(false)` (VERIFIED-HEADER: `withAutomatable` exists in `juce_AudioProcessorValueTreeState.h`) so it is not offered to host automation lanes
  - `link` (String, default "") and `outputFolder` (String absolute path, default `File::userMusicDirectory/LinkGrabber`) are properties on a child `ValueTree` of the APVTS state, so `copyState/replaceState` + `createXml` persist everything in one blob via `getStateInformation/setStateInformation`
  - These extras are message-thread only. The worker never reads the tree; it receives copies at job start
  - Restore rules: invalid XML keeps defaults; choice index clamped by APVTS; missing `outputFolder` on disk keeps the stored path (created at download time); empty path uses default; `link` is NOT trusted on restore (re-validated at download time)

### 3. Download Manager (job runner)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::Thread`, `juce::ChildProcess`, `juce::AsyncUpdater`, `juce::Timer`, `juce::ListenerList`, `juce::CriticalSection` (modules `juce_core`, `juce_events`)
- **Purpose:** Run one yt-dlp job (which calls ffmpeg) off the audio and message threads; publish a thread-safe status snapshot; support cancel
- **Parameters Affected:** reads `format` as a copy at start
- **Configuration:**
  - Owned by the PROCESSOR (not the editor) so a running download survives closing the editor window (VERIFIED-PRIOR design). One job per plugin instance; `start()` while busy is ignored
  - Status snapshot `{mode, percent, elapsedSeconds, title, message, filePath, format}` guarded by a `CriticalSection`; worker updates it and calls `triggerAsyncUpdate()`; `handleAsyncUpdate()` (message thread) notifies listeners
  - Modes: `idle, downloading, converting, done, errorTool, errorLink, errorUnavailable, errorNetwork, errorOutdated, errorFailed` (extends prior set; see Failure Mapping)
  - 1 Hz `Timer` ticks elapsed seconds while active
  - Destructor: set cancel flag, kill child, `stopThread(5000)`, `cancelPendingUpdate()`, `stopTimer()`
  - On `done`, the manager does NOT write history itself (worker must not touch UI/shared state); the message-thread listener hands the finished entry to the History Store

### 4. Tool Locator and Tool Manager (yt-dlp, ffmpeg, JS runtime)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::File`, `juce::File::getSpecialLocation(userApplicationDataDirectory)`, `juce::URL`/`juce::WebInputStream` (update download, phase 2.4 only), `juce::ChildProcess` (modules `juce_core`)
- **Purpose:** Find (and later, install/update) `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg` and a JavaScript runtime without relying on the host's PATH
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:** see "Decision D2: Tool distribution" below. Resolution order: (1) managed copy in `~/Library/Application Support/LinkGrabber/bin/`, (2) `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`. Check executable bit with `access(X_OK)` (VERIFIED-PRIOR helper). Child gets an explicit `PATH` via `/usr/bin/env PATH=<managed bin>:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin <tool> ...` because `juce::ChildProcess` has no environment parameter (VERIFIED-HEADER, VERIFIED-PRIOR)

### 5. Download Command, Progress Parser and Failure Classifier (pure, UI-free)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation on `juce::String`, `juce::StringArray`, `juce::URL` (module `juce_core`)
- **Purpose:** Validate the link, build the argv, parse the merged stdout/stderr stream incrementally, classify failures. Header-only and unit-testable without spawning anything
- **Parameters Affected:** `format` (selects ffmpeg args)
- **Configuration:** reuse the design of prior `DownloadCommand.h` (VERIFIED-PRIOR): https-only, host allow-list (`youtube.com`, `www.`, `m.`, `music.`, `youtu.be`), no `@`/`:`/`%` in the authority, no whitespace/control chars, no leading `-`, length <= 2048, argv built as a `StringArray` (never a shell string), `--` before the link. Details in Algorithm Details

### 6. History Store
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::File`, `juce::var`/`juce::JSON` (or `ValueTree`+`XmlElement`), `juce::TemporaryFile`, `juce::InterProcessLock` (module `juce_core`)
- **Purpose:** Persist the download history (title, path, format, timestamp, video id, size) so past downloads can be re-dragged in later sessions and in other plugin instances
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:**
  - File: `~/Library/Application Support/LinkGrabber/history.json`, global to all instances (a user wants history in every new project, so it must NOT live only in the session blob). Schema `{ "version":1, "entries":[{ "id","title","path","format":"mp3|wav","timestamp":ISO8601,"bytes" }] }`, newest first, capped at 200 entries (oldest dropped from the list; files on disk are never deleted by the plugin)
  - All I/O on the message thread (file is a few KB). Writes go through `TemporaryFile::overwriteTargetFileWithTemporary()` (atomic replace). Multi-instance safety: take a short `InterProcessLock("LinkGrabberHistory")` around read-merge-write; merge by `id`+`path` so two instances never clobber each other. Reload on editor open and when the file modification time changes (polled by the editor's 1-2 Hz timer)
  - On load each entry gets a `exists` flag (`File::existsAsFile()`); missing files are shown greyed ("moved or deleted") and cannot be dragged; offer "Remove" per row. Never auto-prune silently
  - Corrupt JSON: rename to `history.corrupt-<time>.json`, start empty, never crash

### 7. File Drag-Out Source (native)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::DragAndDropContainer::performExternalDragDropOfFiles` called from a native `juce::Component::mouseDrag` (module `juce_gui_basics`)
- **Purpose:** Let the user drag the finished file (or any history row) onto a DAW track/arrangement or Finder
- **Parameters Affected:** none
- **Configuration:**
  - VERIFIED-HEADER signature: `static bool performExternalDragDropOfFiles(const StringArray& files, bool canMoveFiles, Component* sourceComponent = nullptr, std::function<void()> callback = nullptr)`. Use `canMoveFiles = false` (copy semantics; the file in the output folder must remain the source of truth for history), `sourceComponent = this` (the draggable component itself)
  - Call it from `mouseDrag` once the pointer has moved >= 4 px from mouse-down, exactly once per gesture (guard flag cleared in the callback and on `mouseUp`). Do not delay with `callAsync`/timers: on macOS JUCE requires the live event (see Decision D1)
  - Only enabled for entries whose file exists. Drag payload is the real file in the output folder, never a temp copy (hosts often keep a reference, and a vanished temp file breaks the clip)

### 8. Minesweeper Board and Controls (native UI)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioProcessorEditor`, `juce::Component`, `juce::Timer`, `juce::TextEditor`, `juce::ComboBox`/toggle via `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState::ComboBoxAttachment`, `juce::FileChooser`, `juce::SystemClipboard`, `juce::File::revealToUser` (modules `juce_gui_basics`, `juce_graphics`, `juce_audio_processors`)
- **Purpose:** Link field + Paste, format selector, Download/Cancel, LED counters, smiley, tile grid showing progress, draggable result, scrolling history list, output-folder chooser, Show in Finder
- **Parameters Affected:** `format`
- **Configuration:** drawn with `juce::Graphics` (custom `paint`, no images required). Grid is a fixed matrix (for example 16 x 6 = 96 tiles; final size set by the mockup): `revealedTiles = round(percent/100 * N)` during `downloading`; a distinct sweep during `converting` (flood-reveal a wave across remaining tiles); `done` clears the board and shows a sunglasses smiley; any error flips one tile to a mine, shows a dead smiley and the message. 30 Hz `Timer` runs ONLY while a job is active or a reveal animation is playing. The editor listens to the `DownloadManager` and the `History Store`, never owns them. Mockup is not yet created: layout and pixel metrics are deferred to the mockup (`/dream LinkGrabber`)

## Processing Chain

```
AUDIO THREAD (all it ever does):
  Host input buffer ──> processBlock (in place, untouched, zero latency) ──> Host output buffer

MESSAGE THREAD:
  Editor (native JUCE UI)
    ├─ link field / Paste ──> state tree (link)
    ├─ format selector    ──> APVTS "format" (non-automatable)
    ├─ Download ──> DownloadManager::start(link, format, outputFolder)   [copies, no tree access]
    ├─ Cancel   ──> DownloadManager::reset()  (kill child)
    ├─ mouseDrag on result / history row ──> performExternalDragDropOfFiles(file)
    └─ listener(downloadStatusChanged) ──> repaint board / counters / smiley
                                  ▲
                                  │ AsyncUpdater (message thread)
BACKGROUND THREAD (juce::Thread "LinkGrabber download"):
  validate link ─> locate tools ─> ensure output folder ─> ChildProcess:
     /usr/bin/env PATH=... yt-dlp [args] -- <link>        (yt-dlp spawns ffmpeg)
  loop: readProcessOutput ─> Progress Parser ─> snapshot (CriticalSection) ─> triggerAsyncUpdate
  on exit: resolve final path ─> snapshot(done | error*)
                                  │
MESSAGE THREAD (on done):         ▼
  History Store::add(entry) ──> atomic write ~/Library/Application Support/LinkGrabber/history.json
```

**Routing notes:**
- No audio-thread interaction with any non-audio component. No atomics or lock-free queue are needed between them and `processBlock`.
- No feedback, no parallel audio path, no sidechain, no MIDI, no latency compensation.
- Cross-thread data: status snapshot (mutex, microsecond holds, never from the audio thread) and the `AsyncUpdater` trigger. History file is touched only on the message thread.

## System Architecture

### File I/O System
**File types:** `.mp3` (320 kbps CBR via ffmpeg/libmp3lame) and `.wav` (PCM 24-bit little-endian, `pcm_s24le`) written by ffmpeg under yt-dlp's control; `history.json`; `LinkGrabber.log`. The plugin never decodes or reads audio.
**Loading strategy:** none; the plugin only verifies the produced file exists.
**JUCE classes:** `File`, `FileChooser` (folder pick, async), `TemporaryFile`, `InterProcessLock`.
**Thread safety:** folder creation and existence checks on the worker; chooser, reveal, history I/O on the message thread; audio thread never does file I/O.
**Error handling:** folder not creatable/writable gives `errorFailed` "Cannot write to the output folder" before any spawn (VERIFIED-PRIOR). Filename template `%(title).140B [%(id)s].%(ext)s` includes the video id, so repeated downloads of the same video collide deterministically (yt-dlp skips/overwrites; behaviour must be tested, see Risks).

### Multi-Output Routing
Not applicable (single stereo in, single stereo out).

### MIDI Routing
Not applicable.

### State Persistence
**Per instance (inside the host session):** APVTS state XML containing `format`, plus child tree `{link, outputFolder}`. Download status and the last finished file are runtime only.
**Global (shared by all instances/sessions):** `history.json` and the managed tools folder, both under `~/Library/Application Support/LinkGrabber/`.
**Serialization:** `copyXmlToBinary(state.createXml())` / `replaceState(ValueTree::fromXml(...))` after checking the tag name.
**Restore behavior:** see Core Component 2.

## Parameter Mapping

LinkGrabber has exactly ONE parameter. It performs no audio processing; it only selects the output format of the next download. Source: `parameter-spec-draft.md` (no mockup exists yet; no design-sync conflicts to report).

| Parameter ID | Type | Range / Choices | Default | Automatable | Controls |
|--------------|------|-----------------|---------|-------------|----------|
| `format` | `AudioParameterChoice` | 0 = MP3 320 kbps, 1 = WAV 24-bit | 0 (MP3 320 kbps) | No (`withAutomatable(false)`) | Download Manager ffmpeg arguments for the NEXT job; no DSP effect |

Format to yt-dlp arguments:

| format | Arguments |
|--------|-----------|
| 0 MP3 320 | `-x --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 320K` |
| 1 WAV 24-bit | `-x --audio-format wav --postprocessor-args "ffmpeg:-c:a pcm_s24le"` |

Non-parameter state (not exposed to the host): `link` (String), `outputFolder` (String), history list (file, global).

Changing `format` while a job runs does not affect that job (copies taken at start).

## Algorithm Details

### yt-dlp command line (VERIFIED-PRIOR: ran successfully end to end in console tests)

```
/usr/bin/env PATH=<managed bin>:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin \
  <yt-dlp> --ignore-config --no-playlist --no-colors --newline --progress \
  --progress-template "download:LGP %(progress._percent_str)s" \
  --print after_move:filepath \
  --ffmpeg-location <dir of ffmpeg> \
  --paths <outputFolder> --output "%(title).140B [%(id)s].%(ext)s" \
  -x <format args> -- <link>
```

Notes:
- `--ignore-config` prevents a user's yt-dlp config from changing behaviour. `--paths` + a relative `--output` avoid the `%` escaping problem of putting the folder into the template (prior reference choice). `--no-playlist` stops `&list=` links downloading a whole playlist.
- The `LGP <percent>` prefix lets the parser pick progress out of a merged stdout/stderr stream. The final path is the last absolute-path line printed by `--print after_move:filepath`; accept it only if it is an existing file whose parent is the output folder; otherwise fall back to the newest `.mp3/.wav` in the folder modified since job start (WEB: yt-dlp issue #6939 reports odd `after_move` behaviour in some combinations).
- Optional duration guard (phase 2.3): `--match-filter "duration <= 3600"` so a 10-hour livestream cannot fill the disk; expose later as a setting only if the mockup asks.
- Honest content note: YouTube audio is already lossy (AAC/Opus). MP3 320 and WAV 24-bit are containers/transcodes, not a quality gain. WAV 24-bit must be checked with `ffprobe` (`codec_name=pcm_s24le`) in phase 2.2 (VERIFIED-PRIOR that the console test used it; the ffprobe assertion is still a required check).

### Progress model
1. `LGP nn.n%` line: percent = max(previous, floor(value)); never decreases within a job.
2. Percent reaching 100 while `downloading`: mode becomes `converting` (ffmpeg stage; the board runs its sweep animation because ffmpeg gives no percent).
3. Final path line recorded.
4. Process exit: exit code 0 and a resolvable file gives `done`; anything else is classified.
5. A 1 Hz timer keeps the elapsed counter alive when yt-dlp prints nothing.

### ChildProcess semantics (VERIFIED-HEADER / posix source in JUCE 8.0.12, VERIFIED-PRIOR)
- stdout and stderr are merged when both flags are set; prefixes are therefore necessary.
- `readProcessOutput` blocks until data or EOF. The worker cannot poll `threadShouldExit()` while blocked; cancel works by setting a flag and `kill()` (SIGKILL on the direct child), after which the worker thread itself sees EOF and exits. Never read from another thread after `kill()`.
- `kill()` hits only yt-dlp; an ffmpeg grandchild can survive as an orphan and `.part`/temp files remain. Mitigation: on cancel/failure delete `*.part`, `*.ytdl`, `*.temp` files created since job start; if orphans show up in testing, swap the spawner for `posix_spawn` + `setpgid` + `killpg` behind a small `ProcessRunner` interface (not needed for v1 unless the test finds orphans).
- JUCE forks in a multithreaded host. This is how JUCE has always spawned children and is accepted practice, but is a low-probability hazard.

### Failure mapping (extends VERIFIED-PRIOR classifier)

| Mode | Triggers (lower-cased text from the last ~25 output lines) | User message |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------|
| `errorLink` | validation fails (no process spawned) or `unsupported url`, `is not a valid url`, `incomplete youtube id` | "Invalid link: paste a YouTube URL" |
| `errorUnavailable` | `private video`, `video unavailable`, `members-only`, `not available in your country`, `age-restricted`, `sign in to confirm your age` | "Video unavailable, private or age-restricted" |
| `errorNetwork` | `getaddrinfo`, `temporary failure`, `network is unreachable`, `timed out`, `unable to download webpage`, `connection` | "Network error: check your connection" |
| `errorOutdated` | `sign in to confirm you're not a bot`, `http error 403`, `unable to extract`, `nsig`, `no supported javascript runtime`, `requested format is not available` | "YouTube changed: update yt-dlp" (shows Update hint) |
| `errorTool` | tool not found / spawn failed | "yt-dlp or ffmpeg not found" |
| `errorFailed` | anything else; folder not writable; exit 0 but no file | "Download failed (see log)" |

Age-restricted videos normally need an authenticated session (cookies). Passing browser cookies (`--cookies-from-browser`) is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (privacy and TCC implications); the message tells the user. The log file `~/Library/Logs/LinkGrabber.log` (512 KB cap, truncate-on-overflow) stores the last output lines; the UI never shows raw tool output.

### Link validation
As in Core Component 5: parse the host with `juce::URL` and compare to the allow-list, not `contains("youtube.com")`. The link is ONE argv element after `--`.

### Minesweeper mapping
Percent to tiles: `n = floor(percent/100 * N)`; reveal order is a fixed shuffled sequence seeded by the job so the board looks organic but is deterministic for tests. Error: the tile at the failure point becomes a mine; smiley dead; message line. Done: all tiles revealed with numbers cleared, sunglasses face, result row becomes draggable.

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- Download Manager depends on Tool Locator (before spawn), Command/Parser (during), path resolution (after).
- History Store depends on Download Manager's `done` event (via message-thread listener).
- Drag-Out depends on a finished file (current job or history entry that still exists).
- Editor depends on Download Manager and History Store through listener interfaces only (no ownership), so closing the editor never affects a running job.
- Tool Manager (phase 2.4) feeds Tool Locator.

### Parameter Interactions
- None between parameters (only one). State interactions: `format`/`link` changes during a job apply to the next job only. `reset()` and `start()` both go through the Download Manager, the single place that enforces one job at a time.

### Processing Order Requirements
1. Validate link (no process yet) -> 2. locate tools -> 3. create output folder -> 4. spawn and read to EOF -> 5. resolve final file -> 6. publish `done` -> 7. (message thread) add to history -> 8. enable drag.
Audio passthrough is independent of all of this.

### Thread Boundaries
- **Audio thread:** `processBlock` only.
- **Message thread:** editor, state tree, FileChooser, clipboard, reveal, `performExternalDragDropOfFiles`, History Store I/O, listener notifications.
- **Worker thread:** locate/validate, spawn, blocking read, parse, snapshot writes. Never calls UI, tree or history APIs.
- **Communication:** `CriticalSection` snapshot plus `AsyncUpdater` (not `callAsync` with raw `this`, because the processor-owned manager can outlive the editor).
- **Second process boundary:** the host may run the plugin out-of-process (Logic AU hosting, Bitwig); everything above stays inside the plugin's own process, so no change.

---

## Implementation Risks

### R1. Drag-out into DAWs
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM-HIGH (host-dependent, UNVERIFIED in any DAW).
**Risk factors:**
1. VERIFIED-HEADER (`juce_Windowing_mac.mm`): the mac implementation uses `[[view window] currentEvent]` and starts an `NSDraggingSession` on the source component's `NSView`. It needs a live mouse-down/drag event, so it must be called synchronously from `mouseDrag`. If `sourceComponent` is null it looks for the component under the mouse and can assert.
2. WEB (JUCE forum: "[WebView] Drag and drop audio files out of plugin"): with a WebView the call hit an assertion unless a source component was passed; HTML5 drag cannot supply files to other apps; there is no cross-platform way to drag binary files out of web views other than images. A drag from a plain JUCE component avoids all of that.
3. WEB (JUCE forum): one developer saw Studio One drops that worked only sometimes while the call reported success. Per-host acceptance is not guaranteed.
4. Host behaviour (ALL UNVERIFIED, test in phase 2.0): Ableton Live accepts audio files dropped on tracks/arrangement and supports MP3 and WAV; Logic Pro accepts file drops on the tracks area (but its AU may be hosted out-of-process via `AUHostingServiceXPC`, so the drag session originates from a remote view; this is the single most uncertain case); Reaper accepts file drops onto tracks/arrangement and is typically the most permissive; FL Studio accepts file drops on the Playlist/Channel Rack (Windows path); Bitwig accepts drops onto tracks (and may sandbox plugins out-of-process). Commercial plugins that drag audio files out (sample browsers and loop libraries) show the approach is generally feasible in these hosts (general knowledge; not verified per host).
5. VST3 vs AU on macOS use the same `NSView` drag path; Windows uses OLE drag (`DoDragDrop`) for both. No format-specific JUCE code.
**Alternative approaches:**
1. Standalone app drag (works with the DAW since it is a separate app window).
2. "Show in Finder" and "Copy file path / Reveal" so the user can drag from Finder.
3. Offer a `File > Add to Project` hint (hosts have no API for this; not feasible).
**Fallback architecture:** keep Show in Finder always present. If a host fails the drag, document it ("use Show in Finder, then drag from Finder"). No architectural change needed.
**Mitigation:** Phase 2.0 spike right after the Stage 1 shell: a native component dragging a dummy `.wav` and `.mp3` from the plugin editor, tested in Standalone, Logic Pro (AU), Ableton Live (VST3 + AU), Reaper (VST3 + AU). Record a per-host table in the plan before building the history UI.

### R2. Host sandbox / exec / write permissions
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM (partly retired by VERIFIED-PRIOR).
**Risk factors:** VST3/AU v2 run in the host process and inherit its sandbox. Logic AU (out-of-process) ran `/usr/bin/true`, `yt-dlp --version`, `ffmpeg -version` and wrote to `~/Music/LinkGrab` successfully (VERIFIED-PRIOR). Ableton/Reaper/Bitwig are not App Sandbox apps (UNVERIFIED each). AUv3 app extensions and Mac App Store hosts (GarageBand, Logic from App Store is not sandboxed in the same way) are unsupported targets. TCC prompts appear when writing to Desktop/Documents/Downloads/external volumes and are attributed to the host app; default `~/Music/LinkGrabber` avoids this. A real network download inside a host has NOT been tested.
**Fallback:** Standalone-only operation for any host that blocks exec/network, plugin remains a harmless passthrough.
**Mitigation:** phase 2.2 includes a host smoke test of a real download (short public-domain video) in Logic, Ableton and Reaper before the GUI is polished.

### R3. Tool bundling, signing, updating
**Complexity:** MEDIUM-HIGH. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM (design choice D2 contains it).
See Decision D2. Key points: nested executables inside a signed VST3/AU bundle must each be signed inside-out; modifying a signed bundle breaks its seal, so a bundled yt-dlp cannot be updated in place; the plugin bundle location may be root-owned (`/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins`); Python-based/PyInstaller yt-dlp binaries need hardened-runtime entitlements (`disable-library-validation`, `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`) to run when signed with hardened runtime (WEB, PyInstaller-on-macOS general guidance; UNVERIFIED for yt-dlp specifically).
**Fallback:** v1 relies on Homebrew-installed tools (known working, VERIFIED-PRIOR); the managed folder is added later without changing the Download Manager.

### R4. yt-dlp / YouTube breakage and JavaScript runtime
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** HIGH over time (outside our control).
**Risk factors:** YouTube changes frequently break extraction; yt-dlp 2025.11.12 added external JavaScript runtime support and YouTube without one is deprecated (WEB: yt-dlp EJS wiki and release notes); Deno is enabled by default, other runtimes need `--js-runtimes`; the official PyInstaller binaries bundle the EJS scripts but NOT the runtime (WEB). A DAW's PATH lacks `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so deno is not found unless PATH is passed (VERIFIED-PRIOR). Bot checks ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot") can appear on some networks (WEB).
**Fallback:** `errorOutdated` mode with an actionable message; log file; an "Update tools" action (phase 2.4) running `yt-dlp -U` (standalone binary only; Homebrew copies must use `brew upgrade yt-dlp`, WEB: release binaries update only within their channel, `--update-to nightly` available).
**Mitigation:** save real output samples as parser test fixtures in phase 2.2; pin a tested yt-dlp version in the plan notes; run a daily-or-on-launch "yt-dlp --version" only when the user opens the editor (no background network).

### R5. Legal / Terms of Service
**Complexity:** LOW (technical) / **Risk Level:** HIGH (non-technical).
Downloading from YouTube may violate YouTube's Terms of Service, and downloading copyrighted material without rights may infringe copyright. yt-dlp itself is Unlicense (public domain); ffmpeg is LGPL/GPL depending on build (WEB, general knowledge) so redistributing a bundled ffmpeg brings licence obligations (source offer/notices; a GPL build with libx264 etc. is not needed, but common static builds enable GPL parts). Mac App Store and most plugin marketplaces would reject this product. Recommendations: keep this a personal-use tool; do not publish or sell; first-run notice that the user is responsible for having rights to the content; restrict hosts to YouTube; no playlist/channel downloads; keep the duration guard. This is a product decision for the user, recorded here, not blocked by the architecture.

### R6. Worker lifetime and cancellation
**Complexity:** MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** MEDIUM. Blocking read, SIGKILL only on the direct child, plugin destroyed mid-download, partial files. **Fallback:** `ProcessRunner` with `posix_spawn` + process group kill. **Mitigation:** 10x open/close test including mid-download close plus a `ps` check for stray `yt-dlp`/`ffmpeg`.

### R7. History file integrity and multi-instance writes
**Complexity:** LOW-MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** LOW. Atomic replace + `InterProcessLock` + merge-by-id; corrupt file quarantined. **Fallback:** per-instance in-memory history if the lock cannot be taken (log and continue).

### R8. Native UI polish (Minesweeper look)
**Complexity:** LOW-MEDIUM. **Risk Level:** LOW. Custom `paint` bevels; the prior LinkGrab UI was never rendered visually, so verify with real screenshots in Stage 3. Timer runs only when needed (CPU).

### Overall Project Risk
**Overall complexity:** MEDIUM (many small components, no algorithm of research-grade difficulty).
**Highest-risk components:** drag-out into specific DAWs (R1) and YouTube/yt-dlp drift (R4). Both are environmental and can only be settled by testing / maintenance.
**Recommended approach:** Stage 1 shell; drag spike first (phase 2.0); then engine with Homebrew tools; then history; managed tools last.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### D1. Native JUCE UI, not WebView
**Decision:** Draw the board and controls natively (`juce::Component`/`Graphics`); no `WebBrowserComponent`.
**Rationale:**
- Drag-out is the headline feature. `performExternalDragDropOfFiles` needs the live mouse event and a real `Component` source. A WebView would have to bridge JS mousedown to a native call (late, unproven; JUCE forum reports assertions/silent failures) and a JUCE component cannot overlay a native WKWebView for hit-testing (VERIFIED-PRIOR: that was the reasoning that led LinkGrab to drop WebView after Stage 0).
- The Minesweeper look is simple tiles, bevels and LED digits, cheap to paint natively; no CSS needed.
- No `NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER`, no resource-provider/interop-script pitfalls (patterns #8, #9, #13, #21), smaller risk surface in hosts (WKWebView-in-plugin focus/keyboard quirks, Paste via `SystemClipboard` works natively).
- Only one parameter, so WebView relay/attachment infrastructure gives no benefit.
**Alternatives considered:** WebView with native drag strip (works but splits UI in two worlds); WebView with JS-triggered drag (unproven).
**Tradeoffs:** native painting means more C++ drawing code and no live HTML mockup reuse (the mockup, when made, is a visual spec, not code).

### D2. Tool distribution (yt-dlp, ffmpeg, JS runtime)
**Decision:** Phased.
1. v1 (Stage 2 phases 2.2-2.3): discover Homebrew/system tools; pass explicit PATH; clear error if missing. (Working, VERIFIED-PRIOR.)
2. Phase 2.4 (optional, for non-technical users or distribution): a Tool Manager that keeps tools in `~/Library/Application Support/LinkGrabber/bin/` (user-writable, survives plugin reinstall, not part of the signed bundle). Seeds: either download on first run (`juce::URL`/`WebInputStream` from the official yt-dlp release and a pinned ffmpeg static build, verify SHA-256) or copy from `Contents/Resources` of the plugin bundle on first run. Updates: `yt-dlp -U` for the standalone binary (WEB: release binaries self-update within their channel).
**Why NOT embed-and-run-inside-the-bundle:** a signed `.vst3`/`.component` seal breaks if its contents change; the install folder can be root-owned; each nested Mach-O needs inside-out signing and hardened-runtime entitlements; yt-dlp must be updated every few weeks. Why not Homebrew-only forever: requires Terminal skills and Homebrew on every machine.
**Architectures:** Apple Silicon + Intel. Use the official universal macOS yt-dlp build if present (WEB: the yt-dlp release lists a macOS standalone executable; confirm it is universal2 in the release assets at implementation time) and arm64 + x86_64 ffmpeg static builds combined with `lipo`, or choose the build matching `uname -m` at install time. Never assume `/opt/homebrew` (arm64) vs `/usr/local` (Intel): both are searched.
**Signing/notarization:** personal use with ad-hoc signing (repo workflow, critical pattern #18; sign WITHOUT `--deep`) needs no notarization. For distribution: Developer ID, hardened runtime, sign nested binaries first, notarize and staple the installer/bundle. Files fetched by the plugin itself via `juce::URL` are not quarantined and so are not Gatekeeper-assessed (UNVERIFIED but standard for non-browser downloads); run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` on them anyway, as a belt-and-braces step.
**JS runtime:** treat `deno` (or QuickJS) as a required third tool for reliable YouTube extraction; include it in the managed folder or pass `--js-runtimes deno:<path>`.

### D3. Processor-owned download manager
A running download must survive the editor closing (hosts create/destroy editors freely). The manager is a processor member, listeners come and go. (VERIFIED-PRIOR design.)

### D4. Global history file, per-instance session state
History must survive across projects and instances, hence a file in Application Support rather than the host session blob. Format and link live in the session so a project reopens as left.

### D5. Parameter vs plain state for `format`
`AudioParameterChoice` (non-automatable) gives standard APVTS persistence and ComboBox attachment, and matches the contract (`parameter-spec-draft.md`). Link/folder are not parameters.

### D6. No shell, ever
argv array, `--` separator, strict URL validation, folder only from state (never from JS or text input), paths for drag/reveal only from worker/history entries.

---

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- Audio thread: nothing but passthrough. No locks shared with other threads.
- Snapshot lock is held only for struct copies; never held while reading from the child or calling listeners.
- `FileChooser` kept as a member and guarded with `Component::SafePointer` (editor may close while the dialog is open).
- Destruction order: stop timers, cancel job, join worker, cancel pending async update, then release listeners.

### Performance
- Idle cost: zero timers while no job and no animation; editor refresh only on status change.
- Download CPU is in external processes; limit one job per instance.
- History list: at most 200 rows, painted lazily (`ListBox`).

### Denormals
Not applicable (no arithmetic on audio).

### Sample Rate Handling
Not applicable to the passthrough. Downloaded files keep the source sample rate chosen by ffmpeg (typically 44.1/48 kHz); no resampling to the project rate is done; the DAW handles conversion on import.

### Latency
0 samples. Nothing to report to the host.

### Security
Untrusted input is the link text (and clipboard). Validated in C++, passed as a single argv element after `--`. Output folder only from `FileChooser` / default. Never log full environment. Log contains links and tool output tails only.

### Platform scope
macOS (VST3 + AU + Standalone) first. Windows/Linux would need a different tool locator, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` handling and drag via OLE; not in scope for v1.
